prompt.adult: Ezekiel is taken to the gateway and sees a man. According to 40:3, what was that man’s appearance like?
prompt.child: A man met Ezekiel at the gateway with a measuring tool. What did the man look like?
prompt.teen: Ezekiel 40:3: “a man whose appearance was like” what?
prompt.older: According to Ezekiel 40:3, what was the man’s appearance like?

verses.text: He took me there, and behold, there was a man whose appearance was like the appearance of bronze. He had a line of flax and a measuring rod in his hand, and he stood in the gateway.

explanation.child: Look right after “appearance was like” in verse 3.
explanation.teen: 40:3 describes the man, then his tools. Read the first description.

teaching.extended_explanation: 40:3 also says he had a line of flax and a measuring rod in his hand, and he stood in the gateway.
teaching.takeaway: His appearance was like the appearance of bronze.

prompt.adult: Ezekiel 40:4 tells him to look, hear, and fix his mind on everything shown him. In 40:1, after naming the dates, how does the verse say the hand of the LORD came upon him?
prompt.child: Ezekiel dates this vision carefully, then marks the moment. How does 40:1 say that moment came, once the dates are given?
prompt.teen: Ezekiel 40:1: “on the very same” what, “the hand of the LORD was upon me”?
prompt.older: Read with 40:4, how does 40:1 say the hand of the LORD came upon him, once the dates are given?

verses.text: In the twenty-fifth year of our captivity, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was captured, on the very same day the hand of the LORD was upon me; and He took me there.

And the man said to me, “Son of man, look with your eyes and hear with your ears, and fix your mind on everything I show you; for you were brought here so that I might show them to you. Declare to the house of Israel everything you see.”

explanation.child: Look just before “the hand of the LORD was upon me” in verse 1.
explanation.teen: 40:4 is the charge to look and hear; 40:1 then marks the moment. Read that phrase.
explanation.older: It comes just before “the hand of the LORD was upon me” in 40:1.

teaching.extended_explanation: 40:1 also names the opening dates of the vision. 40:4 says, “Declare to the house of Israel everything you see.”
teaching.takeaway: It was on the very same day.

prompt.adult: Ezekiel 43:12 says, “This is the law of the temple.” In 43:10, after they may be ashamed of their iniquities, what are they to do with the pattern?
prompt.child: The man tells Ezekiel to describe the house to the people, that they may be ashamed. What are they then to do with the pattern?
prompt.older: Read with 43:12, what does 43:10 say they are to do with the pattern?

verses.text: “Son of man, describe the temple to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities; and let them measure the pattern.
This is the law of the temple: The whole area surrounding the mountaintop is most holy. Behold, this is the law of the temple.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 10.
explanation.teen: 43:12 states the law of the temple; 43:10 ends with what they are to do. Read the end.

teaching.extended_explanation: 43:10 also says, “describe the temple to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities.” 43:12 says the whole area surrounding the mountaintop is most holy.

prompt.adult: Ezekiel 44:17 says they shall put on linen garments in the inner court. In 44:1, when he is brought back to the outer gateway of the sanctuary that faces east, what does the verse say of it?
prompt.child: Ezekiel was brought back to the outer gateway of the sanctuary that faces east. What does the end of 44:1 say of it?
prompt.older: Read with 44:17, what does 44:1 say at the end?

verses.text: Then He brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary which faces toward the east, but it was shut.

And it shall be, whenever they enter the gates of the inner court, that they shall put on linen garments; no wool shall come upon them while they minister within the gates of the inner court or within the house.

explanation.teen: 44:17 describes the priests’ linen garments; 44:1 ends with the state of what he was shown. Read the end.

teaching.extended_explanation: 44:1 also says he was brought back to the outer gateway of the sanctuary that faces east. 44:17 says no wool shall come upon them.

prompt.teen: Ezekiel 47:14: “You shall inherit it” how “with one another”?
prompt.older: Read with 48:30, how does 47:14 say they shall inherit it?

verses.text: You shall inherit it equally with one another; for I raised My hand in an oath to give it to your fathers, and this land shall fall to you as your inheritance.
“These are the exits of the city. On the north side, measuring four thousand five hundred cubits

explanation.child: Look right after “inherit it” in verse 14.
explanation.teen: 48:30 begins the north-side measurements; 47:14 states how they inherit. Read that word.

teaching.extended_explanation: 47:14 also says, “this land shall fall to you as your inheritance.” 48:30 begins the north-side measurements of the city.

prompt.adult: Ezekiel 40:2 says he was set on a high mountain. In 43:11, if they are ashamed of all they have done, he is to make known the design of the temple and its arrangement, and also what, named just after that?
prompt.child: If the people are ashamed of what they have done, Ezekiel must make the design known. What two things does the verse name just after “its arrangement”?
prompt.teen: Ezekiel 43:11: “its arrangement,” then what two things, “its entire design and all its ordinances”?
prompt.older: Read with 40:2, what does 43:11 name just after “its arrangement”?

verses.text: In the visions of God He took me into the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain; on it toward the south was something like the structure of a city.

And if they are ashamed of all that they have done, make known to them the design of the temple and its arrangement, its exits and its entrances, its entire design and all its ordinances, all its forms and all its laws. Write it down in their sight, so that they may keep its whole design and all its ordinances, and perform them.

explanation.child: Look right after “its arrangement,” in verse 11.
explanation.teen: 40:2 is the mountain vision; 43:11 lists what to make known. Read the next pair.

teaching.extended_explanation: 43:11 also says, “if they are ashamed of all that they have done.” 40:3 says the man stood in the gateway.
teaching.takeaway: He is to make known its exits and its entrances.

prompt.adult: Ezekiel 43:6 says he heard Him speaking from the temple. In 44:18, after naming linen turbans and linen trousers, what shall they not clothe themselves with?
prompt.child: The priests had rules about what they could wear while they served. What does the verse say they shall not clothe themselves with?
prompt.teen: Ezekiel 44:18: “they shall not clothe themselves with” what?
prompt.older: Read with 43:6, what does 44:18 say they shall not clothe themselves with?

verses.text: Then I heard Him speaking to me from the temple, while a man stood beside me.
They shall have linen turbans on their heads and linen trousers on their bodies; they shall not clothe themselves with anything that causes sweat.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 18.
explanation.teen: 43:6 is the speaking from the temple; 44:18 ends with what they must not wear. Read the end.

teaching.extended_explanation: 44:18 also says they shall have linen turbans on their heads and linen trousers on their bodies. 43:10 says they may be ashamed of their iniquities.
teaching.takeaway: They shall not clothe themselves with anything that causes sweat.

prompt.child: The priests had a teaching task among the people. Besides the holy and the unholy, what were they to help the people discern between?
prompt.teen: Ezekiel 44:23: “and cause them to discern between” what?
prompt.older: Read with 48:8, between what does 44:23 say they shall discern?

choices.text: the strong and also the weak
the first and also the last
the near and also the far

verses.text: “And they shall teach My people the difference between the holy and the unholy, and cause them to discern between the unclean and the clean.

by the border of Judah, from the east side to the west, shall be the district which you shall set apart, twenty-five thousand cubits in width, and in length the same as one of the other portions, from the east side to the west, with the sanctuary in the center.

explanation.teen: 48:8 describes the set-apart district; 44:23 ends with what they must discern. Read the end.

teaching.extended_explanation: 44:23 also says they shall teach the difference between the holy and the unholy. 48:8 says the district is set apart from the east side to the west.
teaching.takeaway: They shall discern between the unclean and the clean.

prompt.adult: Ezekiel 47:21 says they shall divide this land among themselves according to the tribes of Israel. In 48:35, after the distance all the way around, what shall the name of the city be from that day?
prompt.child: The last line of Ezekiel gives the city’s name. What shall the name of the city be from that day?

verses.text: “Thus you shall divide this land among yourselves according to the tribes of Israel.
All the way around shall be eighteen thousand cubits; and the name of the city from that day shall be: THE LORD IS THERE.”

explanation.teen: 47:21 is the charge to divide the land; 48:35 ends with the city’s name. Read that name.

teaching.extended_explanation: 48:35 also says, “All the way around shall be eighteen thousand cubits.” 47:21 says, “according to the tribes of Israel.”
teaching.takeaway: The name of the city shall be THE LORD IS THERE.

prompt.teen: Ezekiel 48:31: “one gate for Reuben, one gate for Judah, and one gate for” whom?
prompt.older: Read with 43:1, for whom is the third north one in 48:31?

verses.text: Afterward he brought me to the gate, the gate that faces toward the east.
(the gates of the city shall be named after the tribes of Israel), the three gates northward: one gate for Reuben, one gate for Judah, and one gate for Levi;

explanation.child: Look at the last name in verse 31.
explanation.teen: 43:1 says he was brought toward the east; 48:31 lists the three northward openings. Read the third name.
explanation.older: It follows “and one gate for” at the end of 48:31.
